headline: Approved prior meeting minutes; reports covered measles cases, the Resource Center, and department activity.
summary: The meeting covered a measles update, wastewater surveillance in Nashua, and reports from the director and city departments. The only recorded decision was approval of the September minutes. No public comment was made.

Page 1 of 4 
 
 
 
Board of Health 
October 14, 2026 
18 Mulberry Street 
Nashua, NH 03060 
12:30 PM 
Our mission is to promote, protect, and preserve the health and well-being of the Greater Nashua Region 
through leadership and community collaboration. Our vision is to have an informed, safe, healthy, and 
resilient community where all people can thrive and prosper. We subscribe to the following values: integrity, 
leadership, adaptability, and respect. 
Facilitator: Board Chair, Dr Charles 
Cappetta   
Minutes 
Attendees 
Board of Health (BOH):  Dr. Charles Cappetta, Stephanie Ballentine, Christian Jimenez; 
Henry Och 
Board of Alderman:  
City Employees: Bobbie D Bagley, Director DPHCS; (Via Zoom) Mike McGuiness, Deputy 
Health Officer; Flavia Martin, Deputy Chief Public Health Nurse, Bob Mack, Welfare 
Officer; Foqia Ijaz, CS Administrative Assistant; Sakshi Gurung, Epidemiologist  
Updates and Announcements 
Meeting Called 
to Order 
 
Board Chair, Dr. Cappetta called the meeting to order at 12: 30 P.M referencing NH RSA 
91-A:2, II.  
Approval of 
Minutes 
September, 
2026 
• Approved   
Epidemiologist 
Report 
Presented by 
Sakshi Gurung 
• The United States is experiencing an increase in measles cases, with approximately 
4080 confirmed and suspected cases reported across 47 states as of October 8, 
2026, the highest total in 35 years. The increase is attributed to both interstate and 
local transmission, declining MMR vaccination rates, and an increase in travel-
related cases.
Page 2 of 4 
 
• Five deaths were reported among unvaccinated individuals. One additional death 
was reported by the media but had not been reflected on the New Hampshire 
Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) dashboard. The CDC reported 
two deaths and continued to review the cases. A discrepancy in the reported 
numbers was noted. New York declared a statewide disaster emergency related to 
measles.  
• Updates on measles cases in Mexico and Canada were also given. 
• Respiratory Illnesses: CDC data showed low levels of respiratory illness in New 
Hampshire. COVID-19 activity was also low. 
• Wastewater Surveillance: Nashua showed elevated and increasing levels, while 
Merrimack remained low and stable. 
• Updates were provided on completed activities, meetings, and other epidemiology 
initiatives. 
Questions and Discussion 
• What is the status of wastewater surveillance in Nashua? The recent DHHS 
dashboard provides data for several major cities. A link will be shared so members 
can review the trends. It was noted that wastewater surveillance is now being 
conducted in Nashua by the Wastewater Department. 
Director’s Report  
Presented by 
Bobbie Bagley, 
Director DPHCS 
• DPHCS vision and mission were read.  
• Update from the National Association of Local Boards of Health (NALBOH) 
conference was given. Conference materials and resources will be shared. 
• Received a $10,000 award from the Endowment for Health to support intentional 
conversations called IZI’s that help to provide information on various initiatives. 
• Proof of Concept: Legislation passed by Aldermen to approve lease agreement with 
Harbor Care for implementing Resource Center. A press release was sent out, and 
the Director thanked Harbor Care for their support. 
• The feasibility study report for the Resource Center was presented at City Hall. The 
study will help secure the $1.2 million in federal funding for the project. 
• Updates were provided on participation in the Homelessness Gap Committee. 
• The director was nominated for an advocacy award in recognition of the 
department’s work by the New Futures Policy Committee. 
Community Services Department Highlights 
• Community Health Workers (CHWs): Reported 831 client interactions during the 
reporting period, involving various types of services, including job application 
assistance. In one case, a family lost a member who had been paying the 
household bills, resulting in utility expenses exceeding $22,000. Staff worked with 
utility companies, enrolled the family in assistance programs, and connected them 
with a church payee to help manage payments. 
• Housing Services Officer (HSO): Increased the number of clients receiving Tenant-
Based Rental Assistance (TBRA) due to housing instability. 
• Public Health Emergency Preparedness (PHEP): Staff completed CPR instructor 
training and will provide training to other staff members. 
• Resource Center staff have been hired, and planning for the warming station 
continues.
Page 3 of 4 
 
Questions and Discussion 
• The Board Chair congratulated the director on receiving the advocacy award. 
• What is HMIS? A: The Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) is a 
coordinated data system that allows participating agencies to share information 
and coordinate services for individuals experiencing homelessness. 
• Will a mobile clinic be available at St. Joseph Hospital for the Resource Center? 
Partners have not yet been contacted about visiting the Resource Center. This may 
be explored as the center becomes busier. Information on the opening of the 
Resource Center has been provided to the partner organizations so that they can 
refer clients.  
CH Department 
Report provided 
by Deputy Chief 
PH Nurse Flavia 
Martin 
 
• Supporting nursing students during their six-week rotations. 
• Staff attended the Wheels on Wings event. 
• Flu clinics were held at various agencies. 
• The pharmacy inspection was completed successfully. 
Environmental 
Health (EH) 
Department 
report provided 
by Deputy Health 
Officer –Mike 
McGuiness 
• September was a busy month. Staff absences affected the number of inspections 
completed. 
• Some inspections and investigations required additional time, particularly when 
sites were close to receiving a ticket or required further compliance work. 
• Temporary events continued to generate a high volume of work, including 
weekend activities. Staff will assess whether weekend coverage is feasible. 
• Complaints included mice, rats, and mold.  
• Pools and spas were quieter, and indoor pool sampling is beginning. 
• One cat tested negative for rabies. Two dog bites were reported. 
• Coordination continued with Code Enforcement, Building, and Fire departments on 
environmental health concerns. Issues involving owner-occupied properties remain 
challenging because of legal limitations on available interventions. 
• A food service establishment voluntarily closed following a sewage backup. The 
issue was resolved. 
• An educational presentation was planned at Nashua High School South.  
• Staff are preparing for the fall Environmental Health conference. 
Welfare 
Department 
report provided 
by Bob Mack, 
Welfare Officer  
• Spending remained relatively stable. Shelter assistance continued to be the largest 
expense, primarily to prevent homelessness. 
• Welfare provides rental assistance and refers clients to other agencies for 
additional support. 
• HMIS primarily tracks services for individuals experiencing homelessness; 
therefore, Welfare has relatively few cases recorded in the system. 
• A comparison of FY26 and FY27 was given, including client numbers, inquiries, and 
voucher totals. Spending remained within budget expectations. 
• Staff continue to work closely with CHWs to connect clients with resources, 
including TBRA program.
Page 4 of 4 
 
• Staff attends wraparound meetings to address complex client needs and identify 
service gaps. 
• Staff training and committee participation updates were provided. 
Other Updates  • The November 11, 2026 meeting was moved to Wednesday, November 18 as 
November 11th is a holiday. 
Public Comment 
 
 
 
 
• No public Comments 
 
The meeting adjourned at 1:15 PM following a motion and vote. 
 
Please join us for our Next Meeting: 
November 18, 2026 at 12:30 PM
